incident.title: [DEMO C041] Airtable authentication links fail for late arrivals
incident.description: Older Airtable connection links show expiry errors for returning users, while fresh connections work, reducing onboarding completion.

tasks.question: Scope and coordinate the evidence-led incident investigation.

Starting with null filters, what canonical records exist for Airtable authentication initiation/callback failures during 2026-11-12T09:50:00Z to 2026-11-12T10:15:00Z, and can we segment by link age, tenant, request outcome, latency, and backlog to compare expired-link failures versus fresh successful connections?

Were there any changes around the incident window to the auth-link generation, expiry policy/TTL, redirect handling, tool-executor auth handoff, or Airtable-related configuration/dependencies, and is there evidence tying a change to only older links while leaving newly created links healthy?

Does the evidence support authentication_initiation_expired for older Airtable links more strongly than alternatives such as oauth_redirect_uri_mismatch, provider_failure, credential/configuration issues, or an internal regression, based on a controlled comparison between failed old-link attempts and successful fresh-link attempts?
Challenge the diagnosis, evidence grounding and verification gaps.
Write the evidence-backed internal report and proposed next steps.

events.question: Starting with null filters, what canonical records exist for Airtable authentication initiation/callback failures during 2026-11-12T09:50:00Z to 2026-11-12T10:15:00Z, and can we segment by link age, tenant, request outcome, latency, and backlog to compare expired-link failures versus fresh successful connections?

Were there any changes around the incident window to the auth-link generation, expiry policy/TTL, redirect handling, tool-executor auth handoff, or Airtable-related configuration/dependencies, and is there evidence tying a change to only older links while leaving newly created links healthy?

notes: Canonical records in the incident window show one Airtable auth failure and one comparison success in tool-executor logs: cedar request req-41 at 2026-11-12T10:05:00Z returned 410 with connection_state=EXPIRED, initiation_age_seconds=950, completion_window_seconds=600, and token_exchange_attempted=false, indicating the request failed before provider token exchange (ev_547deced8d61 / airtable-expiry-041:logs:0). A same-time maple log shows status 200 and same_provider_available=true, unrelated_read_succeeds=true as a healthy comparison outcome, though it is not a canonical auth-callback record (ev_547deced8d61 / airtable-expiry-041:logs:1).

Observed segmentation favors link-age as the discriminator: the failed cedar request used an older initiation age of 950s versus a 600s completion window (ev_547deced8d61 / airtable-expiry-041:logs:0). A controlled sandbox comparison matches that mechanism: original condition with initiation_age_seconds=950 produced status 410, connection_state=EXPIRED, token_exchange_attempted=false, while corrected condition with initiation_age_seconds=120 produced status 200, connection_state=ACTIVE, token_exchange_attempted=true (ev_ad0020a530a7 / airtable-expiry-041:reproduce:0, ev_ad0020a530a7 / airtable-expiry-041:reproduce:1).

Tenant impact and performance differ sharply at 10:05Z: cedar had 636 requests, 390 failures (~61%), 390 business operations blocked, queue_depth 114, and p95 latency 1520ms, while maple had 538 requests, 0 failures, queue_depth 0, and p95 latency 160ms (ev_4978f845ca13 / airtable-expiry-041:metrics:0, ev_4978f845ca13 / airtable-expiry-041:metrics:1). This supports tenant-localized impact rather than uniform provider outage, but does not by itself prove backlog caused the expired-link failures.

Important gaps/counter-evidence: there are no canonical initiation-creation or callback-series records beyond the single expired cedar request, so coverage of all late-arrival/fresh-auth attempts is incomplete. Dependency data says provider_api_reachable=true (ev_6a9ad25ec4f4 / airtable-expiry-041:dependencies:0), and there was no tool-executor deployment in 09:00-10:30Z (ev_2c1be0296f9d), which weakens provider-wide outage and immediate executor-release explanations; however, missing broader auth-flow telemetry means alternative contributors such as session-policy behavior or clock issues are not fully excluded.

No observed incident-window change is tied to tool-executor auth handoff: the tool-executor deployment query for 09:00–10:30 returned no records (ev_2c1be0296f9d), and the only deployment found overall was an unrelated support-dashboard release at 10:05 (ev_9f5257ec4a0a, airtable-expiry-041:deployments:0).

Canonical executor evidence matches an age/TTL boundary affecting older links while fresh links remain healthy: cedar failed with 410 EXPIRED at initiation_age_seconds 950 versus completion_window_seconds 600, and token exchange was not attempted (ev_547deced8d61, airtable-expiry-041:logs:0). In the controlled sandbox comparison, the 'original' aged initiation (950s) failed the same way, while the 'corrected' fresh initiation (120s) succeeded and did attempt token exchange (ev_ad0020a530a7, airtable-expiry-041:reproduce:0; ev_ad0020a530a7, airtable-expiry-041:reproduce:1).

Observed scope is tenant-specific rather than a broad Airtable/provider outage: cedar saw 390 failures out of 636 requests, 390 blocked operations, queue_depth 114, p95 latency 1520 ms (ev_4978f845ca13, airtable-expiry-041:metrics:0), while maple had 0 failures out of 538 requests, queue_depth 0, p95 latency 160 ms, and a same-provider read succeeded (ev_4978f845ca13, airtable-expiry-041:metrics:1; ev_547deced8d61, airtable-expiry-041:logs:1).

Important gap: there is no canonical evidence here of a change to auth-link generation, redirect handling, TTL/session policy, auth-service deployment, or Airtable-specific configuration; the dependency records only show tool-executor depends on auth-service/provider-api/session-policy and provider API was reachable (ev_6a9ad25ec4f4, airtable-expiry-041:dependencies:0). The empty auth-service dependency query (ev_dcf087f64f7f) does not verify absence of auth-service changes, so a change-driven explanation remains unconfirmed.

notes: Evidence supports authentication_initiation_expired more strongly than oauth_redirect_uri_mismatch, provider_failure, credential/configuration failure at the Airtable boundary, or a demonstrated tool-executor regression for the observed request.
Backlog/latency in cedar are real but are not shown to be the immediate mechanism of the EXPIRED response; the observed request already exceeded the 600s window.

hypothesis.description: Observed Airtable auth failures are more strongly explained by expired authentication initiations for older links than by redirect mismatch, provider failure, or a broad internal regression. The failing flow is already past its 600s completion window, returns EXPIRED/410, and never attempts provider token exchange; a controlled comparison shows the same aged initiation fails while a fresh initiation succeeds.
assumptions: The cedar failures are representative of the reported 'older link' population, though only one canonical expired auth request is shown.
The sandbox controlled comparison verifies age/window as a discriminating variable for the stated scenario, not every possible production path.

findings.statement: A canonical production request failed with 410 EXPIRED at initiation_age_seconds=950 against a completion_window_seconds=600, and token exchange was not attempted.

In the controlled comparison, the aged initiation (950s) failed with 410 EXPIRED and no token exchange, while the otherwise matched fresh initiation (120s) succeeded with ACTIVE state and token exchange attempted.
The failing production request did not reach provider token exchange, which makes provider-side Airtable failure a weaker explanation for this observed failure.
Fresh connection behavior is healthy in the controlled comparison, and a same-time comparison tenant also shows success.

Impact is substantial but localized: cedar saw 390 failures out of 636 requests with 390 blocked operations, queue depth 114, and p95 latency 1520ms, while maple saw 0 failures out of 538 requests with queue depth 0 and p95 latency 160ms.
Provider-wide unavailability is weakened by provider_api_reachable=true and a same-provider comparison success in maple.

actions: Have users start a fresh Airtable authentication initiation and complete it within the valid window instead of retrying expired links.
Collect canonical auth-flow telemetry linking initiation creation time, callback receipt, and expiry decision for affected late-arrival attempts.
Align auth-flow and executor telemetry windows so old-link failures and fresh-link successes can be counted directly by initiation age.
missing_checks: Canonical initiation-creation and callback-series records for the affected production links are not present, so the exact population of old-link failures versus fresh-link successes is not fully measured.
No canonical auth-service or session-policy records show whether a clock/policy change altered the effective expiry decision for these links.

hypothesis.description: A redirect URI mismatch is possible in OAuth flows generally, but current evidence does not support it as strongly here because the observed failure is EXPIRED before token exchange, and fresh initiations succeed in the controlled comparison.
assumptions: A true redirect URI mismatch would usually need callback/config evidence not present here.

findings.statement: The observed failing request stops before token exchange and is labeled EXPIRED, which does not specifically indicate redirect URI mismatch.
When only initiation freshness is changed in the controlled comparison, the result flips from EXPIRED/410 to ACTIVE/200, reducing the need for a redirect-mismatch explanation.
There are no canonical callback or OAuth app configuration records here to directly verify or rule out redirect URI mismatch.

actions: If redirect mismatch remains a concern, verify the OAuth app callback URI against the auth configuration using canonical callback/config records.
Capture callback-stage errors separately from initiation-expiry decisions so redirect failures are distinguishable from expired-link failures.
missing_checks: Canonical callback error/configuration records are missing; those records could materially confirm or dismiss redirect mismatch for the affected links.

hypothesis.description: An internal regression or configuration/policy change is not demonstrated by current evidence. There is no observed tool-executor deployment in the incident window, but missing auth-service/session-policy change telemetry prevents fully excluding a non-executor internal contributor.
assumptions: An internal contributor, if any, may sit in auth-service or session-policy rather than tool-executor itself.
The absence of a tool-executor deployment does not prove no internal change elsewhere.

findings.statement: There was no observed tool-executor deployment during 09:00-10:30, and the only deployment found was an unrelated support-dashboard release.
Tool-executor depends on auth-service and session-policy, but no canonical change records for those dependencies are provided here.
Missing auth-service or session-policy deployment/config telemetry leaves an internal change explanation unconfirmed rather than disproved.

actions: Collect deployment/configuration history for auth-service and session-policy covering initiation TTL, clock source, and callback expiry handling.
Separate executor-local failures from dependency policy decisions in logs so future incidents can distinguish expired links from internal policy regressions.
missing_checks: Auth-service and session-policy deployment/config records are unavailable; they could materially change whether an internal change contributed to the expiry behavior.

findings.statement: The only canonical failed Airtable auth request shown is already beyond its allowed completion window and returns EXPIRED without attempting token exchange.
A controlled original-versus-corrected comparison isolates initiation age as the changed variable and reproduces failure for the old initiation while succeeding for the fresh one.
Observed production impact is concentrated in cedar, not uniform across tenants: cedar has 390/636 failures and blocked operations, while maple has 0/538 failures.
Coverage is incomplete because canonical initiation creation, callback-series, and dependency change records are missing for the broader population of reported old-link and fresh-link attempts.

events.question: Challenge the diagnosis, evidence grounding and verification gaps.

notes: The evidence is sufficient to approve a bounded diagnosis for the observed failed execution: ev_547deced8d61 / airtable-expiry-041:logs:0 shows a production 410 EXPIRED at initiation_age_seconds=950 versus completion_window_seconds=600, with token_exchange_attempted=false, and ev_ad0020a530a7 / airtable-expiry-041:reproduce:0 and :1 provide a discriminating control where age flips the outcome.

The report correctly weakens provider-side Airtable failure for this observed request because the failure occurs before token exchange; same-time comparison health in maple and provider_api_reachable=true further reduce a provider-wide outage explanation within observed scope (ev_547deced8d61 / airtable-expiry-041:logs:1, ev_4a6de2586239 / airtable-expiry-041:dependencies:0).

Impact is properly scoped as localized rather than global: cedar has 390/636 failures, queue_depth 114, p95 1520ms, while maple has 0/538 failures, queue_depth 0, p95 160ms (ev_4978f845ca13 / airtable-expiry-041:metrics:0 and :1).

The candidate should be read narrowly: current evidence verifies expired initiation as the immediate mechanism for the observed failed auth flow, not the deeper reason many cedar requests were in that state. Missing auth-service/session-policy change records are a caveat about upstream cause, not a blocker to diagnosing this execution.

One statement should be interpreted carefully: the maple log is a useful healthy comparison but not direct proof of fresh auth-link success in production, since ev_547deced8d61 / airtable-expiry-041:logs:1 is an unrelated successful same-provider operation. The stronger freshness control is the controlled reproduce evidence, not that maple record.

No material contradiction currently undermines the leading explanation. The absent auth-service/session-policy telemetry could change attribution of why expiries were prevalent, but would not overturn the observed pre-provider expiry mechanism for req-41.

missing_checks: Auth-service and session-policy deployment/config records are unavailable; they could materially change whether an internal change contributed to the expiry behavior.

findings.statement: A canonical production Airtable auth request failed with 410 EXPIRED at initiation_age_seconds=950 against completion_window_seconds=600, and token exchange was not attempted.

In the controlled comparison, the aged initiation at 950s failed with 410 EXPIRED and no token exchange, while the otherwise matched fresh initiation at 120s succeeded with ACTIVE state and token exchange attempted.
The observed failed request did not reach provider token exchange, so provider-side Airtable failure is a weaker explanation for this execution.
Observed evidence weakens a provider-wide outage explanation: provider_api_reachable=true, and a same-time comparison tenant had a successful same-provider operation.

Impact is substantial but localized. Cedar had 636 requests with 390 failures and 390 blocked operations, queue depth 114, and p95 latency 1520ms, while maple had 538 requests with 0 failures, queue depth 0, and p95 latency 160ms.

The affected tenant also showed elevated queue depth and latency during the window, but the observed failed request was already past its completion window, so backlog is observed context rather than the demonstrated immediate mechanism.
No tool-executor deployment was observed in the incident window, and the only deployment found overall was an unrelated support-dashboard release.

Tool-executor depends on auth-service, provider-api, and session-policy, so dependency-side policy or TTL behavior could still matter even though the immediate observed mechanism is expired initiation.

Important causal coverage is missing because canonical initiation-creation, callback-series, and dependency change records are not present for the broader population of reported old-link and fresh-link attempts.
